subject: [PATCH v3 08/11] mm, swap: only charge physical swap entries

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that zswap and physical swap should not be treated as competing resources, agreeing to expand on this reasoning in the next version.

Author acknowledged that they are working on implementing Johannes Weiner's feedback about swapoff path and per-vswap spinlock, promising to report back if issues arise.
reviews.raw_body:
I agree, and yeah I should have been clearer about the reasoning in
this patch commit message itself. I made the argument in a response to
Kairui's inquiry in the past, but forgot to include it here. My
apologies - will expand on this in the next version.

It really does not make sense to make zswap and phys swap competes for
the same limit, when they don't compete for a tangible resource (zswap
consumes memory, where as phys swap consumes storage space).

---

Acked. I'm trying to implement this. Will report back if something
doesn't work, but otherwise it will be in the next version.

2026-08-10.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory management to only charge physical swap entries when they acquire actual backing, rather than immediately upon allocation. This change ensures that memory.swap.current accurately reflects on-disk swap usage and prevents zswap-backed pages from being counted as occupying swap space. As a result, cgroups with all pages in zswap can now reclaim anonymous memory even if memory.swap.max is set to 0.
